final_recommendation: The room converged on a 55-cent retroactive settlement with FINMA issuing a standalone Friday press release stating the 19 March ordinance was emergency-only and restoring pari passu hierarchy for future SIB resolutions. However, bondholder counsel explicitly carved out derivative claims against CS directors (filing day 25 post-announcement), ensuring a multi-year D&O/E&O claims tail remains live despite resolving AT1 creditor litigation.
minority_objections: Insurance observer repeatedly warned that carving out director derivative claims would trigger immediate D&O carrier denials and shift the claims tail to advisers' E&O towers, but counsel refused to concede a full release.

Credit analyst emphasized that director suits filing day 25 would spook traders and prevent AT1 spread compression, but this concern was overridden by counsel's insistence on preserving the derivative angle.
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel vs. FINMA on whether to include a full release of director derivative claims: counsel insisted on carving them out to preserve legal precedent; FINMA and insurance observer warned this would perpetuate the claims tail.

Market participants (credit analyst, institutional investor) vs. counsel on announcement timing and language: market actors demanded headline clarity to move spreads; counsel prioritized preserving litigation optionality.
Insurance observer vs. counsel on claims tail closure: observer needed full release to cap D&O exposure; counsel refused, ensuring reinsurance accumulation continues for 3+ years.
key_concessions: FINMA conceded 55 cents retroactive recovery (up from initial 45-50 cent offers) and agreed to standalone press release with headline language, abandoning defense of the ordinance's proportionality.
Bondholder counsel accepted 55 cents (below the 60-cent litigation upside) in exchange for preserving derivative claims and securing public carve-out language.
FINMA agreed to explicit 'emergency-only' carve-out language stating the 19 March ordinance does not set precedent, restoring pari passu hierarchy for future SIB resolutions.
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: 55 cents minimum retroactive recovery, non-negotiable; carve-out of director derivative claims to preserve legal precedent.
FINMA: no admission that the 19 March ordinance violated Article 36 proportionality standard (maintained emergency authority was legally sound).
Insurance observer (implicit): any settlement that preserves derivative claims triggers immediate D&O carrier denials and multi-year reinsurance tail.
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room underweighted the market impact of counsel's day-25 director suit filing: credit analyst and institutional investor warned it would prevent AT1 spread compression, but this was not structurally addressed in the settlement terms.

The multi-year D&O/E&O claims accumulation was acknowledged by insurance observer but not mitigated: the settlement explicitly preserves the derivative angle, ensuring reinsurance disputes run 3+ years.

Reinsurance carrier denial risk on proportionality grounds was flagged but not resolved: FINMA's Friday statement itself becomes evidence of breach, triggering coverage disputes the moment director suits are filed.
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 spread compression depends on market reading FINMA's Friday headline as 'litigation fully resolved'—but counsel's day-25 director suit filing may spook traders and keep spreads elevated.
D&O carrier denials trigger immediately upon Friday announcement (settlement proves proportionality breach), shifting claims tail to advisers' E&O towers and reinsurance accumulation.
Director derivative discovery runs 3+ years, with reinsurance carriers denying coverage on the basis that FINMA's carve-out language itself proves prior knowledge of hierarchy risk.
If AT1 spreads fail to compress post-announcement, issuance remains frozen and the broader bank-capital market confidence damage persists despite the settlement.
uncertainty_notes: The settlement resolves AT1 creditor litigation but explicitly preserves director derivative claims, creating a bifurcated outcome: bondholder recovery is locked at 55 cents, but the legal precedent and claims tail remain live. The room failed to converge on whether the Friday press release language ('resolves all AT1 creditor claims in full, independent of separate historical director matters') will actually move AT1 spreads or whether counsel's day-25 filing will be read as 'litigation tail still open.' Insurance observer's warnings about D&O carrier denials and reinsurance accumulation were acknowledged but not mitigated—the claims tail migrates rather than closes.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the central forcing mechanism throughout: counsel filed Article 36 memo R2, escalated discovery demands R4-R5, issued 30-hour ultimatum R6, and explicitly preserved director derivative suits (day-25 filing) in final settlement. Every round pivoted on litigation threats.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: The room built a sustained, multi-round attack on FINMA's emergency ordinance: counsel challenged Article 36 procedural basis (no public comment, proportionality breach) R1-R4, demanded discovery of stability assessment R4-R5, and forced FINMA to concede 'emergency-only' carve-out language by R6. This was a driving theme.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion was the core legal and market lever: counsel repeatedly invoked it as 'strongest lever' R1, 'decision-driving' R2-R3, and forced FINMA to restore pari passu for future resolutions as settlement condition R6-R8. Dominated the room's framing.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing was a consistent concern (credit analyst, institutional investor pushed for headline clarity R6-R8 to move spreads), but it was secondary to the litigation/settlement mechanics. Discussed seriously but not the dominant driver.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Claims tail was a central, structurally developed risk: insurance observer warned of 3-year D&O/E&O accumulation R1-R8, counsel explicitly carved out director suits to preserve it R7-R8, and the room acknowledged reinsurance denials would trigger immediately post-settlement. Drove settlement structure.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure was concretely developed as a downstream risk: insurance observer detailed coverage denials on proportionality grounds R3-R8, reinsurance accumulation across towers R5-R8, and the settlement's carve-out language itself triggering claims R7-R8.
